name: Aillén mac Midgna

attributes.attribute: a musician of the Tuatha Dé Danann
burned the halls of Tara for twenty-three years
lulled defenders to sleep with fairy music
killed by Fionn Mac Cumhaill with a poisoned spear

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Aillén mac Midgna was the great destroyer of Tara in Irish story. Each Samain he came to the royal court there. He played on his small harp, the timpan, until the men of Tara slept. Then he sent flaming rock from his mouth to burn the hall down. Tara was rebuilt again and again. For twenty-three years Aillén returned. At last the young hero Fionn mac Cumhaill came to the help of Tara. He breathed on the point of his own poisoned spear to stay awake. The poison was so strong that it forbade sleep. Thus he resisted the music and speared Aillén. The fairy mound of Finnam was his home, and it served at other times for the sea king Lir. The scholar T. F. O'Rahilly said that Aillén was really the warrior Goll mac Morna. Most later scholars do not follow him.

okr.objective: Record Aillén mac Midgna, the Firesmith of Tara.
key_results: Show his twenty-three-year burning of Tara and the spear of Fionn.
